identity.explanation: The supplied pages directly identify 麦わらの一味 (the Straw Hat Pirates) as the pirate crew formed and led by Monkey D. Luffy, and the Wano Country summary follows the crew through its departure from Wano after the raid. The requested continuity is treated as supported by the supplied Wano arc evidence; no adaptation-specific facts are used.

claims.text: The Straw Hat Pirates are a pirate crew formed by protagonist Monkey D. Luffy in the East Blue. After two years of training, they reunited at Sabaody and continued through the New World while pursuing the final island, Laugh Tale.
The supplied crew page lists the members as Monkey D. Luffy, Roronoa Zoro, Nami, Usopp, Sanji, Tony Tony Chopper, Nico Robin, Franky, Brook, and Jinbe.
Jinbe formally joined the Straw Hat Pirates during the preparations for the Onigashima raid in Wano.
The crew page gives the Straw Hat Pirates a combined bounty of 8,816,001,000 berries and identifies June 13 as the crew's commemorative birthday.

The supplied page lists these member Devil Fruits: Luffy has the Gomu Gomu no Mi and Hito Hito no Mi, Mythical Zoan, Model Nika; Chopper has the Hito Hito no Mi; Robin has the Hana Hana no Mi; and Brook has the Yomi Yomi no Mi.
During the Wano conflict, the Straw Hat Pirates were the leading force in an approximately 5,400-person assault on Onigashima, alongside the Heart Pirates, Mink Tribe, and samurai forces.

The Wano summary states that Zoro and the other Straw Hat fighters defeated executives of the Beast Pirates while the allied forces fought Kaido's forces. It does not provide a complete crew-wide combat-style description.
Luffy was defeated or nearly defeated by Kaido, after which a new Devil Fruit power manifested. He used the form called Gear 5 and its described freedom-oriented ability to defeat Kaido.

After Kaido and Big Mom were defeated, the Straw Hat Pirates left Wano and set course for their next island. Luffy's bounty rose to 3,000,000,000 berries and he became recognized as one of the Four Emperors.

The supplied pages contain no named Straw Hat technique beyond the form name Gear 5; the phrase describing Luffy's attack on Holdem is an ordinary description of an angry blow, not an identified formal technique name.
